title: Wipro's Deal Bookings Hit a Near Four-Year Low, Testing Its AI Growth Story
excerpt: Large-deal wins plunged 58.6% to $674 million in the September quarter. Management says two awarded deals simply missed the signature deadline — Q3 will decide whether investors believe that.
body:
• Wipro's total deal bookings fell 22.9% sequentially to $2.6 billion in the September quarter — a near four-year low — while large-deal bookings plunged 58.6% to $674 million.
  • CEO Srini Pallia said two large deals were awarded but not signed before quarter-end and should land in Q3; he called himself "very, very bullish" on December-quarter bookings.
  • The rest of the quarter was steadier: IT services revenue of $2.61 billion was flat, margins rose 50 basis points to 16.5%, and operating cash flow jumped 61.3%.
  • Q3 guidance is muted — revenue between $2.571 billion and $2.625 billion, or -1.5% to +0.5% in constant currency, with seasonal furloughs weighing.

Wipro's growth story now runs through one number: $674 million. That is all the large deals — contracts of $30 million or more — that India's fourth-largest IT services firm booked in the September quarter, down 58.6% from the June quarter. Total bookings fell to $2.6 billion, down 22.9% sequentially and well below the $4.7 billion booked a year earlier, the weakest haul in nearly four years, Livemint reported.

Bookings are the IT industry's forward indicator: deals signed today become billable revenue over the following six to twelve months. A single soft quarter is noise; the question hanging over Wipro is whether the slump delays the AI-led growth narrative the company has been selling since Srini Pallia took over.

Management's answer: the deals exist, the signatures don't — yet

Pallia told reporters that a couple of deals had been awarded to Wipro but were not signed during the September quarter, and are expected to flow into the December quarter. He said he was "very, very bullish" about Q3 bookings, while warning that seasonal furloughs would weigh on third-quarter revenue. The guidance reflects that caution: IT services revenue of $2.571 billion to $2.625 billion for Q3, a constant-currency range of -1.5% to +0.5%.

A steadier quarter underneath

The operational numbers were less alarming than the bookings line. IT services revenue stood at $2,611.5 million, down 0.1% sequentially but up 0.3% year on year, and gross revenue rose 9.1% year on year in rupee terms to ₹24,752.7 crore. Net profit slipped 1.9% year on year to about ₹3,200 crore, largely on lower other income after the June buyback. Operating margin expanded 50 basis points sequentially to 16.5%, and operating cash flow reached ₹5,305 crore, up 61.3%, according to CFOtech's report of the results.

Geography explains part of the strain. The two Americas units — roughly 60% of IT services revenue — contracted year on year, while Europe grew 5.1% and APMEA 13.3%. Pallia pointed to the company's consulting-led, AI-powered strategy and its AI-native unit as the route back to large-deal momentum: "The strategic investments we have been making are beginning to deliver results. They are enhancing our ability to win in new markets, add new clients, and grow existing relationships."

What investors are weighing

The market, for now, is giving Wipro the benefit of the doubt. Its ADRs surged about 5% to a two-month high after the results, helped by a broader rotation into software stocks — the so-called anti-AI trade — though the stock remains down about 34% in 2026 at around ₹174. The December quarter becomes the proof point: if the two unsigned deals close and bookings rebound toward the $4 billion range, the September slump reads as timing. If they slip again, the AI growth story — not just one quarter's pipeline — is what gets repriced. We covered the revenue side of the quarter in our earlier Q2 report.
